verdict.rationale: The only on-topic evidence is a community comment that GitLab is open source at its core, so anyone can run their own instance or fork it. That implies the source is readable under an open license, but only for the core, and the specific license is unnamed. No first-party documentation confirms it. missing for 10: first-party documentation of the source repository and the specific open license, clarity on which parts (e.g., EE features) are not openly licensed, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license

citations.quote: A user values that GitLab is open source at its core, so anyone can run their own instance or fork it if the company moves in a direction the community dislikes.
